Indicator 9 tracks the mortality rate among prevalent patients with atrial fibrillation across [[danmark|Danmark]], comparing performance at the national, regional, and health cluster levels. Monitoring this indicator is critical for assessing the quality of long-term cardiovascular care and identifying geographic disparities in patient outcomes.

Across the reporting periods, the data reveals a steady improvement in survival rates. The national mortality rate stood at 7.3% in the 2024 report [^src1]. By the time of the 2025 report, the national rate had declined to 7.1% [^src2]. This downward trajectory is evident when looking at historical baselines; for example, the national rate was 8.0% in 2021/22 before dropping to 7.6% in 2022/23 and 7.3% in the subsequent period [^src1]. Major regions, including [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] and [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]], mirror this consistent decline across the years [^src1] [^src2].

Despite the overall positive trend, significant geographic disparities persist. [[sundhedsklynge-bornholm|Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]] consistently emerges as the outlier with the highest mortality rates, recording 8.7% in the 2024 dataset [^src1] and 8.5% in the 2025 dataset [^src2]. In the 2024 report, [[klynge-vest|Klynge VEST]] tied with Bornholm for the highest rate at 8.7% [^src1]. Conversely, the lowest mortality rates are found in different clusters depending on the year. [[sundhedsklyngen-holbaek|Sundhedsklyngen Holbæk]] led with the lowest rate at 6.2% in the 2024 report [^src1], while [[sundhedsklynge-nord|Sundhedsklynge Nord]] achieved the lowest rate at 6.3% in the 2025 report [^src2]. 

No explicit target thresholds or met/missed flags are defined in the provided tables, but the continuous year-over-year reduction suggests that systemic improvements in atrial fibrillation management are being realized across most of the country, with the exception of persistently high-risk areas like Bornholm.
